extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists, NGOs, and human-rights practitioners seeking a country-level human rights overview
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic country-level summary of Mali's human rights situation, covering legal protections, institutional practice, specific abuses, vulnerable groups, labor rights, and treaty ratifications. Intended as a reference synthesis of law, government practice, and reported incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for the integrity of the person
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad umbrella assessing protection against arbitrary deprivation of life, disappearances, torture, cruel/inhuman/degrading treatment, and other abuses to bodily integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes constitutional and legal prohibitions and then evaluates government and nonstate actor practice (reports of killings, torture, detention conditions, etc.). Examples include reporting whether government agents committed killings, existence of torture reports, and systemic detention/prison issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary or unlawful deprivation of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the government or its agents committed arbitrary or unlawful killings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate official investigations and prosecutions, cite documented incidents (e.g., Youssouf Dembele found dead in Niono; killing of Assaleh ag Mohamed in Gao; Human Rights Watch documentation of alleged summary executions since Dec 2021). Note whether suspects were detained/awaiting trial and whether the state investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disappearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidence of politically motivated disappearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether there are reports of disappearances; if none, note that explicitly. Check human-rights NGO and government reports for allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torture and other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal prohibition of torture and reports of police or security abuse in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare constitutional/legal bans with reported abuses (police brutality, use of excessive force against demonstrators). Include whether remedies or prosecutions occur and frequency of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison and detention center conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of prison overcrowding, medical care, food supplies, separation of prisoners (by sex, juveniles), pretrial detention practices, and access by monitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document conditions (overcrowded, inadequate medical facilities/food), separation practices, juvenile detention in same facilities, high percentage of pretrial detainees (approx. 77%), and procedures for NGO/prison-monitor visits (requests, delays). Note whether government permits visits and whether delays hinder monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary arrest or detention
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal prohibition of arbitrary arrest/detention and the extent to which authorities observe that prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record occasions of arbitrary arrests (e.g., arrests of high-profile individuals in Dec 2020), whether arrests are used for political control, whether warrants and 48‑hour charging rules are followed, access to counsel, and examples of police misconduct or bribery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the police and security apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure, responsibilities, resources, corruption, training, and accountability of army, gendarmerie, National Guard, and police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe administrative control, district organization, effectiveness, resource/training shortfalls, extortion/corruption patterns, and whether impunity is present (charging/convicting of offending officers; gendarmerie investigating police).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest and detention (procedural safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for arrest (warrants), charging timelines, right to counsel, bail/conditional liberty, and access to family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether warrants are required and properly served, practice (warrants sometimes served for bribes or influential relatives), 48‑hour charge-or-release rule compliance, practical access to lawyers (state-provided if indigent), and instances of detainees held beyond permitted timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of fair public trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of judiciary, executive influence, corruption, resources, and fairness of trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare constitutional guarantees to practical interference (executive influence, appointment/suspension of judges by the minister of justice, Council of Magistrates chaired by president). Include corruption allegations and notable trial outcomes (e.g., acquittals of magistrates in 2005 corruption trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights during trials: public trials, right to counsel, presumption of innocence, access to evidence, right to confront witnesses, appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note exceptions to openness (closed trial of six for 'offending' the head of state), practical obstacles to counsel access due to backlogs and lawyer shortages, and customary/traditional dispute resolution practices in rural areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political prisoners and detainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidence of imprisonment for political expression or politically motivated charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List examples (journalists and high school teacher imprisoned for 'offending' the head of state in June) and whether trials and convictions reflect political motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil judicial procedures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of an independent and impartial judiciary in civil matters and access to remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note existence of independent judiciary in civil matters but also any practical limitations reported in the country; include availability of appeals and civil remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal prohibitions against arbitrary interference and whether the government respects them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether constitution/law prohibit such actions and whether government practice generally respects prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of speech and press
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional guarantees versus limits on press freedom, intimidation, self-censorship, prosecutions of journalists, and instances of harassment or closures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document whether individuals criticize government without reprisal, but also examples of government pressure: arrests and prosecutions for defamation or 'offending' the head of state (e.g., journalists Diaby Macoro Camara and Oumar Bore convicted; teacher Bassirou Kassim Minta arrested), removal of press from courtrooms, fines/suspended sentences, eviction or service cutoffs for broadcasters (Radio Jamakan example), and blanket prohibitions imposed by junta (e.g., 12 April 2024 ban on reporting political party activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on access to and expression on the Internet, government monitoring, blocking of websites, and self-censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record official restrictions (pornography, material deemed objectionable to Islamic values), site blocking by Ministry of Islamic Affairs (e.g., Hilath.com in 2011), absence of credible reports of judicial-overseen monitoring of e‑mail/chat, and prevalence of self-censorship on religion/judiciary reporting. Note disparities in access (numerous Internet cafés in Bamako; limited home access; little access outside capital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic freedom and cultural events
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom for academic institutions and cultural expression; government restrictions on educational/cultural activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note relative freedom except for isolated incidents (e.g., arrest of a high school teacher for an essay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of peaceful assembly and association
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal guarantees for assembly/association and actual government response to demonstrations and formation of associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether government generally respects the right, but include examples of police repression (use of tear gas on journalists' march, injuries), pending trials from protests, and legal prohibitions on associations deemed 'immoral' (used to deny recognition to a gay rights group in 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional protection of religious freedom, registration requirements for public associations, treatment of minority religions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note routine registration for public/religious associations, freedom generally respected, no reports of antisemitic acts, and exceptions for restrictions on groups deemed 'immoral'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of movement and protection of displaced persons, refugees, and stateless persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of movement within and outside the country, protections against forced exile, and systems for refugees and asylum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether constitution/law guarantee movement and foreign travel, note police stops/extortion, prohibition and non-use of forced exile, and mechanisms for refugee protection (1951 UN Convention alignment, national committee, cooperation with UNHCR, temporary protection examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of refugees
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal framework and practical system for granting asylum/refugee status and protection against refoulement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note formal adherence to 1951 Convention and 1967 Protocol, existence of national committee and cooperation with UNHCR, examples of temporary protection for persons not qualifying under convention, and welcome centers assisting repatriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal right to change government peacefully, exercise of political rights, and constraints on political activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document constitutional guarantees and practice (periodic, free, fair elections); note any recent prohibitions (e.g., 11 April 2024 junta prohibition of political party activities) and restrictions necessary for public order as stated by authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections and political participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct of elections, observer reports, party operation, and representation of women and minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record election results and observer characterization (free/fair but administrative irregularities), party operating environment, numbers of women in assembly/cabinet/courts, and representation of historically marginalized groups from northern regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government corruption and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal penalties for corruption, prevalence of corrupt practices, audits/reports, and access to government information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use auditor-general findings (e.g., lost revenues and identified fraud), legal requirements for financial disclosure by cabinet members (not publicly released), existence of public access laws and appeal procedures to administrative court with three-month handling requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governmental attitude regarding external investigation of alleged violations of human rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of cooperation with domestic and international human rights groups and openness to external scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether domestic/international NGOs operate without restriction, and whether government officials are generally cooperative and responsive to investigations and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination, societal abuses, and trafficking in persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of discrimination (social origin, color, language, sex, race), prevalence of violence against women, FGM, child trafficking, and other societal abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate legal prohibitions versus societal practice; cite prevalence of FGM, trafficking in children, forced labor, hereditary servitude, and government/NGO responses or prevention programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women's rights and gender-based violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal protections for women (rape laws), treatment of spousal rape, domestic violence, family law, property/inheritance, access to legal services, employment and education opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that rape is criminalized but spousal rape is legal; domestic violence commonly tolerated; penalties for assault; limited enforcement by police; barriers to women filing complaints; guide produced by Ministry for handling violence; NGOs and shelters present; issues in family law favoring men, limited access to divorce due to costs, unequal traditional practice on inheritance, and women's limited participation in formal labor force (~15%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's rights and welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal protections for children, access to free education (hidden costs), school attendance rates, medical care, child abuse reporting, and child exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record laws (child delegates), tuition‑free education but requirement to buy uniforms/supplies, primary school attendance rates (e.g., 56.6% for ages 7–12 in 2005–06), unreliable abuse statistics, underreported sexual exploitation, and government recommendations to strengthen protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevalence of FGM and government programs to eliminate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that FGM was common (especially rural), performed on girls from six months to six years, and that government programs aimed to eliminate FGM by 2008 (record program targets and timelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking in persons and slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidence of internal and cross-border trafficking for labor, domestic servitude, mining, begging, prostitution, and persistence of hereditary servitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe trafficking patterns (children trafficked to rice fields, mines; girls for domestic servitude; victims from central regions; Nigerian traffickers bringing women/girls), legal prohibitions and penalties (5–20 years, increased for minors), evidence of cases and often-languishing prosecutions, government ministries responsible, international cooperation, welcome centers, and examples of arrested traffickers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence (or absence) of specific laws protecting employment, education, health care, accessibility, and nondiscrimination for persons with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note absence of specific anti‑discrimination law or accessibility mandates, but also lack of reported societal discrimination and Ministry of Social Affairs responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: National, racial, and ethnic minority rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Societal discrimination against Tuareg servile castes and other minority groups, access to identity documents, voter registration, housing, legal protection, and development aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document hereditary servitude (Ikelan/Bouzou/Bella), reported lack of equal educational/civil liberties benefits, discrimination by officials in obtaining ID/voter cards, and reports of thousands still living in enslavement in northern regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBT rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Societal discrimination based on sexual orientation and removal of specific protections in international fora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record societal discrimination and examples (Mali behind removal of specific protections for gays from a UN resolution in 2010), noting citation needs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other social abuses and discrimination (HIV/AIDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Societal discrimination against persons with HIV/AIDS and related social stigmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note existence of discrimination and any reported social consequences or legal protections/shortfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker rights — right of association
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal right for workers to form and join unions, exclusions, and degree of unionization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record that law provides free union formation (excluding military/gendarmerie/National Guard), high unionization among salaried employees (~95%), and absence of reported antiunion activity despite lack of explicit anti-discrimination prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker rights — right to organize and bargain collectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal right to conduct union activities, collective bargaining, and strike rights, plus procedural requirements for strikes by civil servants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe legal protections, exercise of rights, two-week notice and mediation requirements for civil servants and state enterprise workers, prohibition on retribution against strikers, and limited enforcement in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker rights — prohibition of forced or compulsory labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal ban on forced labor (including child forced labor) and reports of continued occurrences and hereditary servitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note law prohibits forced labor and contractual use of persons without consent (penalties include fines and hard labor), increased penalties for minors, and evidence of informal hereditary servitude persisting among ethnic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker rights — prohibition of child labor and minimum age for employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal rules permitting limited child work by age categories and prohibitions in certain contexts, versus widespread child labor in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List legal allowances (ages 12–14 limited hours in vacations; 14–16 limited hours with inspector permission; 16–18 non-physically demanding work with hour caps), sectors with child labor (agriculture, mining, domestic help), gaps in coverage for rural/family work, trafficking in children, and limited enforcement capacity of Labor Inspection Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker rights — acceptable conditions of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum wage, workweek, overtime, occupational safety regulations, and enforcement capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State national minimum wage (approx. $53/month at time cited), required benefit package, legal workweek (40 hours; 45 for agricultural workers), rest period requirements, overtime pay, workplace hazard protections on paper, but weak enforcement especially in informal sector and limited capacity of Labor Inspection Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical situation (Freedom House ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Longitudinal ratings of political rights and civil liberties (Freedom in the World) and status classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Freedom House scores over time (1–7 scale) with status labels (Free/Partly Free/Not Free) to indicate historical trends (examples: 2003 score 2/2; 2012 score 7/5 after unrest). Use the included chart/data as evidence of trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: International treaties and treaty ratifications
rubrics_metrics.description: List of major international human rights treaties Mali has signed/ratified and their status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include treaty names and ratification status/dates (e.g., Genocide Convention, ICCPR, ICESCR, CEDAW ratified 1985, Convention against Torture, CRC ratified 1990, CRPD ratified 2008, etc.). Use treaty status as a metric of formal international commitments.
